claims.text: Stability and self-repair of a passivating surface layer predominantly govern resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys.
Carefully tuned Cr content enables the stability and self-repair of the passivating layer.
A middle-range Cr content in homogenized, as-cast AlCoCrFeNi is suitable for forming passive films.
Cr content will be varied from approximately 5 at.% to 25 at.% while the concentrations of Al, Co, Fe, and Ni are kept constant.
The controlled comparison will use 3.5 wt.% NaCl, approximately 5 N load, approximately 0.2 m/s sliding speed, room temperature, and approximately four hours of testing.
Cr content influences the formation, disruption, and repassivation rates of the oxide-based protective layer.
Higher Cr levels enhance passivation kinetics.
Stable protective oxide films mitigate corrosive attack.
Stable protective oxide films mitigate mechanical abrasion at the sliding interface.
Improved oxide-film stability and repassivation limit net tribocorrosion damage.
Moderate- to high-Cr variants optimized for passivation will have lower combined mass or volume loss than the middle-range-Cr baseline.
Higher-Cr variants will have a lower separately measured corrosion rate than the baseline.
Higher-Cr variants will have shallower wear tracks than the baseline.
Higher-Cr variants will have a lower friction coefficient than the baseline.
The hypothesis may fail in solvents or at pH values where Cr-based passive films are unstable.
The hypothesis may fail when mechanical loading disrupts passive layers faster than they can reform.
The optimal Cr content and its interactions with the other alloying elements are not yet established.
Equal or better combined wear-corrosion resistance in a reduced- or zero-Cr control relative to a high-Cr alloy would falsify the claim that Cr-driven passivation is the primary control.

contradictions.description: Cr atomic percentage cannot be varied from 5 to 25 at.% while all four other elemental atomic percentages remain constant, because the atomic percentages must sum to approximately 100. The intended constraint may instead be a constant relative ratio among Al, Co, Fe, and Ni.

The intervention defines a 5-25 at.% Cr series, whereas the falsification design additionally includes zero Cr and still calls every specimen an AlCoCrFeNi alloy. A zero-Cr specimen is outside the stated series and is nominally an AlCoFeNi control.
